top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori and Ye) rest on a distinct, specific idea, magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms, that opened a regime neither the frequency comb nor single-ion clocks contain and reached 1e-18 uncertainty, confirmed across several independent laboratories after about two decades. The credited claim and the established core coincide, and the two-name allocation (concept and first demonstration, accuracy and systematic control) leaves out no one with a comparably documented claim, which is not true of P001 (Andrei versus Bistritzer) or P003 (Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Hasan). The novelty objection against the 2005 and 2012 prizes is a real weighting judgement but, on content, I regard the lattice principle as distinct. P003 is second as the most mature topology case if confined to the two-dimensional quantum spin Hall effect; P001 third because the phenomena are secure but the field is eight years old, the pairing mechanism is open, and the third seat is contestable; a prize is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: Possible but indirect: I spent time in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder and Jun Ye comes from the JILA frequency-metrology environment around Hall; I also work on laser stabilisation and spectral-hole-burning materials, adjacent to the ultra-stable cavity lasers used in optical clocks. No documented collaboration or institutional tie to Katori, Ye, or the credited names of the topological-insulator and twisted-graphene proposals.
